speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Before we go into the specific amendments of this Bill, I would like to first share with Members the context for AMLA and how it supports our Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even as the British brought English law to Singapore, the British Administration also allowed room for the indigenous inhabitants, the Malay/Muslims, to continue having their personal matters governed by their customs and beliefs, and AMLA continues this practice.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Among the community, there was a strong interest in strengthening the institution of marriage and to nurture stronger families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: So, AMLA also strengthened the Syariah Court (SYC) and the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government continues to maintain this legislative arrangement, which recognises the history and heritage of Malay/Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When the Bill to pass this Act was first introduced in this Parliament in August 1966, then Minister for Social Affairs, Mr Othman Wok, emphasised that the Bill did not seek to deal with substantive Muslim law itself, but its administration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Bill did not seek to deal with substantive Muslim law itself, but its administration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Muslim law derives from Muslim religious sources and the Act does not alter this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Religious guidance and opinion come from the consensus of the asatizah community, led by MUIS, and officially issued by the Fatwa Committee.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This has been so and will always be so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Where AMLA pronounces on religious matters, it serves only to codify the guidance of the ulama.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Religious guidance is reviewed regularly and evolves to address the contemporary challenges that Muslims face.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is to ensure that our laws reflect the prevailing and unique norms of our Singaporean Muslim community, the contemporary expression of our community's faith and address current socio-religious needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At that time, the Government observed that minor marriages were 2.5 times more likely to end in divorce, and consensus was growing that those under the age of 21 were, generally, less prepared for marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Then Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, Dr Yaacob Ibrahim, consulted with the community leaders and the community agreed it was important to signal that minor marriages were discouraged.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many other Muslim communities today still allow minor marriages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we were prepared to look at the evidence, consider contemporary circumstances and adopt norms that made sense for us so that we can stay true to our values of upholding the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MCCY has been working closely with MUIS, SYC, ROMM and other key Muslim stakeholders to review the AMLA.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For this round of reviews, we seek to update the provisions governing the processes and operations of our statutory Muslim institutions, namely MUIS, SYC and ROMM.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Broadly, the amendments seek to enable these institutions to adopt new administrative processes, including digital ones, for greater efficiency and productivity, and keep pace with broader developments in family law, which Minister of State Sun Xueling spoke about on my behalf on 12 January when MSF moved the Women's Charter (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some amendments allow the SYC and ROMM to adopt digital processes so that they can better serve the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have been testing out some of these processes as measures to comply with the safe distancing requirements during the pandemic and we have found that they worked well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are also other amendments that streamline the administration of Muslim marriages and divorces.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Bill also contains amendments to enable MUIS to better administer its functions and duties to support the Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These include amendments to update provisions that are no longer relevant and amendments to enable MUIS' exercise of powers to collect fees for services rendered pursuant to its statutory functions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A draft of this Bill was published for public consultation from 13 August to 10 September 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We appreciated the broad support from the community for this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This became all the more salient with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When the pandemic hit and safe distancing became imperative, the Office of the Mufti issued a religious opinion that the use of live video-link technology to facilitate marriage solemnisations was compatible with Muslim religious law and, thus, to keep everyone safe, ROMM adopted the video-link technology to allow marriage solemnisations to continue.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Similarly, the SYC adapted its Court processes to allow litigants and witnesses to give evidence through approved channels of live video or live telecommunication links, to minimise disruption to divorce proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The pandemic necessitated new norms and habits we did not consider prior to 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The amendments do not replace the traditional mode of physical proceedings but enable SYC, an Appeal Board and ROMM to adopt digital alternative modes of conducting proceedings, if the situation calls for it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is covered by clauses 3, 6, 14, 15, 22 and 23.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Bill also seeks to improve the service experience of Court users.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will provide the legal framework to empower SYC to adopt new IT systems and digital processes, which will improve case management and communication with litigants and their lawyers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond digitalisation, this Bill also seeks to improve legal processes and address past provisions that have inadvertently caused hardship to litigants.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Clause 11 seeks to amend section 50 of AMLA, which governs divorce proceedings conducted by hakam.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The role of a set of hakam is to guide a Muslim couple towards reconciliation and, if it that is not possible, towards an amicable parting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Currently, the parties appoint a set of hakam to support them through this process and the hakam derive their authority from the parties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If one of the parties decides to hold up the process by not giving the hakam the authority to resolve the marital dispute, the SYC can step in to appoint a second set of hakam.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is so that no party can delay registration of a divorce already recognised by the Court under Muslim law through the non-payment of fees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: AMLA confers MUIS with administrative powers to administer key functions of Muslim religious life in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These include the administration of mosques, halal certification and Muslim religious education.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The next set of amendments I would like to highlight seeks to update MUIS' administrative powers, so that they reflect current realities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, clause 17 updates archaic terms, such as "jawantankuasa daerah" and replace them with the more relevant term, "jawantankuasa masjid", while clauses 18 and 19 update AMLA to enable MUIS' exercise of powers to collect fees for the exercise of statutory functions relating to halal certification and the administration of the Asatizah Recognition Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These are the provisions that allow the SYC to advise parents to secure the child's attendance at the Programme for Children during the divorce journey, if the SYC thinks that it would be beneficial, just as the Family Justice Courts now can.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The aim of these provisions, as my colleague Minister of State Sun Xueling explained to the House last month, is to make sure that the best interests of the child are prioritised during the divorce process.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This must be our objective for children of all marriages, whether civil or Muslim.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The amendments do not change the fact that Muslim law will continue to apply to Muslim marriages and divorces.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Deputy Speaker, the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) is a special piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It provides for particular facets of Muslim life in Singapore, including marriage and divorce – alongside other civil laws and rules applicable to non-Muslims – in our secular and plural nation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The proposed amendments, which generally aim to keep the AMLA and its processes up-to-date, are timely and welcome.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In particular, the digitalisation process utilising electronic communications instead of in-person appointments will greatly transform the Syariah Court and the Registry of Muslim Marriages.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, I would like to seek some clarifications from the Minister on certain aspects of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While the Office of the Mufti has issued an irsyad (guidance) that the use of video-conferencing for marriage proceedings is permissible under Islam, I have spoken to several young people who said that a wedding would only be meaningful if it is celebrated in the presence of family and friends.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Hence, I would like to ask, what is the likely take-up rate of this virtual wedding option?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since this option was made available from May 2020, what is the number of couples who have applied for a virtual solemnisation with the Registry of Muslim Marriages, and how does this compare to the number of applications of an in-person solemnisation over the same period?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also note that while couples are now allowed to solemnise their wedding virtually, whereby one condition is that both parties to the marriage, the witnesses and the wali (guardian) of the woman to be wedded must physically be in Singapore, does the Registrar of Muslim Marriages have the discretion to waive this requirement in extraordinary circumstances?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, when the COVID-19 pandemic broke out globally, there were Singaporeans who were stuck overseas and could not return for a certain period of time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If we are harnessing technology to make the solemnisation process easier for Muslim couples who wish to get married, I think it would be helpful to extend this to Singaporeans or Singapore residents who may be abroad at a particular time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, one other concern that I have is whether doing away with the formal, physical attendance before a kadi (solemniser), a wali (guardian) and witnesses would diminish the degree of solemnness and the weight of responsibility that one would attribute to marriage.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is especially pertinent when it comes to teenage and youth marriages, which has long been recognised to be a source of various societal issues, such as high divorce rates, dysfunctional families, drug abuse and juvenile delinquency.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the context of civil marriages, it has been suggested that the Registry of Marriages will have the discretion to ask couples to go through the steps in-person where there may be suspicions of a marriage of convenience, for instance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What would be the circumstances where the Registrar of Muslim Marriages would withhold his/her approval for a virtual solemnisation?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would this include a situation where one or both parties have yet to reach 21 years of age?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On to remote proceedings, as I mentioned earlier, this appears to be a new innovation which goes beyond what COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnization and Registration of Marriages) Act 2020 had provided.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister shed any light on the rationale for the introduction of this innovation at this time?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is it anticipated to form the norm for divorce proceedings in the Syariah Court, or will it remain the exception?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If it is to be an exception, under what circumstances would we see remote divorce proceedings being deployed?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And what would be the impact on Court users, especially when many of them are not represented by lawyers?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In going about our constituency work, I think Members may be familiar with how certain issues can be easily ironed out once parties meet and speak face-to-face, whereas numerous earlier rounds and months of exchanging emails and letters may have done little to move things along.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In moving towards an impersonal approach to divorce proceedings – through remote Court proceedings coupled with the dispensation from having to obtain physical signatures on documents anymore – are we not reducing the opportunities for a disaffected couple to work out their issues and making a final divorce an inevitable conclusion?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What is the expected time saving from doing away with the second set of hakam?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there any statistics on the number of marriages which have been saved from divorce by the second set of hakam?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Two, the Bill also proposes to remove the requirement for the payment of prescribed fees before the Syariah Court must cause a divorce to be registered.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, I very much welcome the amendments which enhance the Syariah Court's power to advise persons to attend counselling and family support programmes in the course of divorce proceedings.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There will now be a clear provision that the Syariah Court may advise one or both divorcing parties to secure the child's completion of a support programme for children.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It cannot be gainsaid that, often, the biggest victims in a marriage that has broken down are the children of the family.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Of no fault of their own, these children lose out on various aspects of family life going forward, at a time when they might not be intellectually mature enough to manage the loss.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Also, would there be further support or "check-ins" with the children beyond the completion of the divorce proceedings, say, one year or two years later?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Bill also provides that the Syariah Court may advise the "prescribed persons" to attend a family support programme or activity beyond the divorcing parties and their children.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Who are these "prescribed persons" that are being contemplated?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Again, what is the expected practical utility if it is not compulsory for such persons to comply with this advice, as the Explanatory Statement spells out?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some final miscellaneous questions in brief, Mr Deputy Speaker.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is this part of a broader plan to overhaul the Syariah Court filing system, to create an electronic filing system like e-litigation?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If so, are there plans to issue guidance to lawyers and litigants-in-person and will the Ministry consider some form of transition period where parties may be exempted from paying extra Court fees if they make inadvertent errors in filing their documents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: More fundamentally, is such a provision necessary since section 32(7) of AMLA already provides that any Court may refer any question of Muslim law to the Legal Committee which the Mufti chairs?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would section 139(2) not usurp the power of the Legal Committee, who must exercise its power through a quorum of not only the Mufti but also two fit and proper Muslims who may also be learned Muslim religious leaders?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, I support this amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In this short speech, I would like to offer my views, seek clarifications and relay my concerns on some issues contained in this amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In addition, I will briefly touch on section 139 of AMLA, relating to false doctrine, although it is not related to this amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, since this issue is an important one and, in the interest of Muslims in Singapore, I would like to highlight this matter in the hope that a change can be made to this section in future.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We have seen at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, many couples who had plans to hold their solemnisation ceremonies and wedding receptions were affected, due to the implementation of the COVID-19 regulations, which were implemented to safeguard the safety and well-being of our people.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Despite the numerous obstacles faced by many couples in the last two years, they do acknowledge that these strict controls are necessary and they bravely and patiently overcame these obstacles so that they can proceed to build a home together.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope and pray that their marriage will last until the end.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I would like to express my concern over the possible undesirable negative impact.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is human nature that any convenience and ease when undergoing a process can influence one's assessment when making a decision.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: For example, based on my past experience in conducting counselling sessions for cases referred by the Court, the divorce process, which can take some time, could sometimes provide more time and space for the divorcing couple to make a deeper assessment before making the final decision to separate.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is because, some married couples make a hasty decision to divorce without much thought because they feel very distressed due to anger and frustration.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I acknowledge that simplifying the Court processes through digitalisation will be good for divorce cases that should be resolved quickly.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These include cases of irrevocable divorce and also cases with elements of domestic violence, where divorce may be the best way out.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In light of these concerns that I have stated, I hope the Syariah Court, in implementing digitalisation processes, can monitor the situation closely to avoid or mitigate any negative consequences arising from these improvements.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Among the feedback received are the use of digitalisation and absence of oral hearings, which can negatively impact the justice process.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is said that such a situation could cause uneasiness because the plaintiffs and the defendants could not witness the process that was carried out, or could not understand how the Court reached its decision.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, it also emphasised that digital channels are not meant to replace existing methods.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I just wish to reiterate that the Syariah Court, the MUIS Appeal Board and the Registry of Muslim Marriages should monitor and take appropriate steps so that there will not be any negative consequences, or at least ensure that any potential undesirable negative impact that may arise when implementing these digitalisation measures is kept as low as possible.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Often, such requests come from wives who do not have any income because they are fulfilling their responsibilities as full-time housewives.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These changes can eliminate that feeling of utter helplessness that is felt by those facing financial issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I believe that the Minister had earlier provided some examples on this matter.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In this matter, I hope the amount of fees charged, if any and if necessary, will not burden the madrasah.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Here, Sir, I would like to declare that I have a child attending full-time madrasah.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The final thing I will be touching on is section 139 which is about false doctrine.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As I mentioned earlier, I would like to raise this matter because it is important.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Any attempt to apply legislation to religious matters must be carefully considered.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In the case of deviant teachings, I previously shared that MUIS seeks to address these problems at the root, by adopting a multi-pronged approach of counselling individuals and inoculating the public against harmful ideologies".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I agree with the approach of addressing issues related to deviant teachings through methods, such as counselling services and public education against the dangers of such ideologies.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I feel that if the punishment for offenders can be further enhanced, it may be a preventive factor and thus strengthen the existing efforts to combat as well as prevent it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope this proposal can be considered again.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: With this, Sir, I end my speech by expressing my support once again for this amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In English): Sir, I support this amendment Bill.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Whether it is working from home, scanning QR codes or managing digital wallets, many of us have become more comfortable with the use of remote technologies and virtual conferencing.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad that we are now making amendments that will, hopefully, bring the same benefits of digitalisation to the Syariah Court or SYC.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are challenges and potential points of amelioration in the transition to digital proceedings from the perspectives of Court, counsel and witnesses.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Safeguards need to be put in place to protect amongst other things, the propriety, solemnity, integrity and orderliness of proceedings.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is important to ensure that each party can express their case independently, fairly with all relevant details.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The complexity of this transition must be tackled head on.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For SYC users and officers who may not find the digitalised processes intuitive, or those who want to use them but face difficulties, what training, resources and support will be available for individuals who need help – in particular, SYC staff or litigants-in-person?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How long will the transition take and how will ongoing cases during this transition be impacted?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, the choice of setting up a dedicated venue to provide a conducive setting for online hearings is left up to the discretion of counsel.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not everyone can afford representation and, even when they can, there may be other prohibitive factors that come into play.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Minister consider establishing a centralised dedicated venue to facilitate this?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are also lessons which we can learn from incidents overseas.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The abuser intended to intimidate his victim to coerce her into adjusting her testimony by being in a position where he could threaten her safety.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: He did this while pretending on screen that they were in two separate locations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It was fortunate in this case that the prosecutor caught on, but, unlike a physical court setting where there are significant safeguards against intimidation, the possibility of a similar scenario in the example earlier is more likely online.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What checks would be in place to prevent such actions from happening?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many of us would have also experienced frustrating technology failures at some point, for example, due to an unstable Internet connection or an issue with the device.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would be important for parties to virtual Court proceedings to be permitted to change to an alternative device if a party encounters video malfunction in the midst of a remote hearing.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Without an actual video feed for corroboration, I would like to ask what safeguards will SYC put in place to ensure that proceedings conducted by electronic means are conducted in a way that is fair to all parties?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For such matters, the judge will be making decisions based on affidavits and submissions only.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In such cases, could the Minister share some examples of proceedings where oral arguments will not be necessary?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I ask this in hopes of getting clarity that there will be little risk for those who are not equipped to provide an affidavit with enough relevant context or details, in particular, any litigants-in-person.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Deputy Speaker, this amendment Bill will have a positive effect on the hearing process, particularly if we encounter complicated situations like a pandemic which prevent certain parties from meeting physically.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, as we strive to implement digital proceedings, it is very important for us to ensure that each party is able to submit statements and get fair and full representation that is free from any threat or intimidation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my speech, I presented three main focus areas.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These include how the Syariah Court can consider several situations where the hearing process may be unsuitable or is not yet suitable to be held online.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In essence, we should be concerned that there are still those within our community who may not be ready for this transition and our digitalisation efforts should facilitate the hearing process from the perspective of certain parties without affecting the safety, protection and rights of each party to seek equitable access to justice.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope this amendment will not result in more pressure or difficulties for certain parties and I hope that adequate preparations, support and resources will be provided for everyone, including Court officials, in this transition.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, a secondary area of clarification I have is with regard to the proposed section 43C, which has been raised in a previous Sitting, as mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These complexities raise questions on who should be making the decisions for the programmes and how they are arriving at them.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are perhaps some of the factors which will be considered in order to accomplish this?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will we make sure that there is also appropriate support and resources for parents?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And if parents prove they are unable to comply with the order, what other steps can be taken?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, Sir, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I declare that I am a practising lawyer.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Allow me to speak in the National Language.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   I welcome the amendments to the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA).

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The amendments update the administration of Muslim marriages and divorces.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It also increases the support given to families who undergo the divorce process, especially children.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is in line with the broader development in family law under the Women's Charter which was recently updated.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Digital processes also allows the Syariah Court and ROMM to leverage on technology, coordinate services and facilitate access to the community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is important to help us prepare for challenges ahead, including any new pandemic in the future.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, the Syariah Court previously did not have an electronic document filing system like the High Court or Family Court.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For roughly a few weeks during the circuit breaker period, no hearings could be conducted because there was no provision for video or online hearings.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Now, the Syariah Court is able to conduct Court hearings and proceedings via video.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, these amendments actually reflect what is being practised in Court, which is the use of video links through WebEx and so on.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These preparations will build greater resilience in the delivery of services by the Syariah Court and thus empower the Syariah Court to deal with new situations in the future.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In my speech on the recent Women's Charter (Amendment) Bill, I highlighted the Syariah Court's experience in successfully incorporating counselling and children-centric programmes to help the divorce process in Court.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With these amendments to AMLA, what other alignments can be made between AMLA and the recently amended Women's Charter in order to better support families and children who are going through divorce?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, I will focus on four areas within the amendments to this Act.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, clarifications on the status of the hakam.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, restriction of access to the Register of Muslim Marriages.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, the Mufti's role in submitting evidence to Court.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is consistent with other changes in civil jurisdiction which allow for determination using documents only in certain cases.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will not only save costs, but also reduce the time needed for a divorce case.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question is, what about a situation where the plaintiff has already given oral evidence but the Defendant subsequently fails or refuses to participate in further proceedings?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Typically, in that scenario, the Court hears the case in absentia of the Defendant and makes the necessary orders, but this means that the plaintiff has to be present, and has to spend time and money to go through an oral hearing.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These amendments also allow the MUIS Appeal Board to decide that oral arguments are not required even if written submissions have been filed.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, I am concerned that a party or parties may feel aggrieved as they did not see the "process" of the appeal or hearing and may not understand why their appeal was dismissed, if all the trial process was held without oral arguments and done through the exchange of documents.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While I am cognisant that in other forums or civil courts, there is a practice of not requiring the attendance of parties at a hearing, however, it is common for MUIS Appeal Board hearings at the moment for the parties to attend and observe the proceedings in full, even though the Court's final verdict will only be published or given a few weeks later.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is the process that lawyers, Courts and parties have been accustomed to when going through the divorce process in Singapore all this while.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, I am worried whether this will impact the perception of parties and society on the adage that it is not just for justice to be done but to be seen to be done because they are unable to observe the proceedings.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help litigants to understand that although there are no oral hearings or arguments, their full cases have been canvassed carefully in the written form.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with the replacement of the terms "arbitration" and "arbitrators" with "hakam" only.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is because arbitration bears a different technical meaning compared to hakam.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also agree with the amendments to allow the Syariah Court to give authorisation to the first set of hakam to pronounce a divorce, should the husband refuse to authorise the hakam to pronounce the divorce.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is because, in certain cases, some wilfully refuse to authorise the hakam or refuse to make payment of the hakam fees and this would further delay proceedings.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There appears to be divergent views by scholars on whether the husband must expressly agree to delegate his "powers" or right to divorce his wife, to the hakam during divorce proceedings.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, I think that it would still be useful to clarify the scope of the hakam's role.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I propose that the definition of "hakam" be included in the amendments, with a clear explanation of the hakam's scope and role – perhaps in the subsidiary legislation – so that the community can understand the hakam's role and accept the decision of the hakam later.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Moving on to the issue of payment to the hakam.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In some cases, there are those who refuse to pay for the hakam's costs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In order to avoid further delays to divorce proceedings, can the Syariah Court order that payment be deducted from the relevant party's share of matrimonial assets or claims?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will allow the divorce proceedings to continue smoothly.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, restriction of access to the Register of Muslim Marriages.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Section 143 previously provides that any party may apply to the Registrar to inspect and obtain copies or extracts from ROMM and Register of Revocation of Divorces.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The rationale stated by MCCY in the Bill Consultation Outcome dated 12 October 2021 is that such restriction of access is "consistent with the broader policies on the protection of personal information".

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with protecting personal data and limiting access to classes of persons as prescribed.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is important because it involves an element of public interest for Muslim marriages here and overseas.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, the bride-to-be or her family from overseas may need proof or access to the marital status of a groom who is Singaporean or who is domiciled in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On the other hand, there are no restrictions to apply for a copy from the Register of Divorces.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would that entry in the Register of Divorces not also contain personal data?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Why is access to the Register of Marriages limited to certain classes of party?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps access to the Register of Divorces should also be similarly limited.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I propose that perhaps the Civil Court procedure for the Request and Order of Inspection of Court documents can be applied.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the civil process, the requesting party has to file a request to inspect and obtain copies of Court documents.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Before being allowed to do so, the party has to provide reasons and, in certain cases, be called before a Registrar to provide sufficient explanation before being given permission to inspect and obtain copies or documents from the Court.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, perhaps the ROMM Registrar can exercise the same standard for requests, whether it is for the Register of Marriages or the Register of Divorces.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Section 139 of AMLA makes it a criminal offence to conduct deviant teachings or anything relating to Islam in a manner contrary to Muslim law.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It also provides for the Court to presume that a doctrine, ceremony or any act is, indeed, contrary to Muslim law if the MUIS President submits evidence that it is so.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I support this because the Mufti is the highest Islamic religious authority in Singapore and chairs our Fatwa Committee.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, the Mufti is better placed to give evidence in Court on Muslim law and the Court will follow the Mufti's evidence.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, I would like to ask why the same could not be applied to section 114 of AMLA in relation to questions of succession and inheritance in Muslim law.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Presently, section 114 of AMLA makes reference to fixed list of religious books.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that this is being considered for the future.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, may I suggest that, just as how section 139 was amended, section 114 of AMLA can also refer to the Mufti if there are questions on Muslim law for inheritance and succession matters.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help make Court rulings more conclusive and consistent.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would also like to repeat my previous suggestion my past speeches, that perhaps the issue of Muslim inheritance and succession, including inheritance certificates, should be dealt with by the Syariah Court instead of the Civil Courts, because it involves Muslim law evidence and public interest that is guided by Islamic teachings.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The AMLA is an important piece of legislation for the Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our reviews are intended to ensure that it remains robust and relevant, stays up-to-date with new programmes and processes, and above all, serves the needs of our Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened by the support from Members and their suggestions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope Members will understand if I focus my responses on the issues directly related to the specific Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, I will not deal with issues on deviant teaching – for which there is a specific case that is under Police investigation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Allow me to summarise the details on the processes that will be digitalised under the SYC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The process of filing and issuing all Court documents will be digitalised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This means that a Court user will be able to file, or submit, documents anytime and from any location using SingPass, or, if they are a lawyer acting on behalf of a party to proceedings, using CorpPass.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Through a fully personalised dashboard upon log-in, a Court user, whether a litigant or a lawyer, will be able to view upcoming Court attendances, outstanding tasks given by the Court and access digital copies of filed documents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This convenience is extended to the pre-Court process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, the registration process to attend the Marriage Counselling Programme will also be digitalised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC and ROMM trialled these video-link processes during the pandemic and the community benefited from them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, this digital option allowed some couples to proceed with the video-link solemnisation even when their witnesses had contracted COVID-19 and, therefore, could not attend in person.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This saved the couples the trouble of postponing the solemnisation, which would incur additional costs and time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During these video-link solemnisations, the Kadi would conduct the same tasks as he would during in-person solemnisations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes confirming the identities and consent of the couples to the marriage, giving a short sermon and supplication, and blessing the couples.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The only difference is that the entire process takes place via live video-link.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For marriage applications involving minors, before a decision is made as to whether virtual solemnisation will be allowed, all parties and their parents must attend in-person sessions with the Kadi, who will assess the couples' readiness for marriage and the level of support from the parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have learned from the various episodes of the COVID-19 crisis in the last two years that disrupted necessary processes even when technological options existed because there were no provisions in law for them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We needed to pass the time-limited temporary provisions to enable these virtually.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, the option to conduct proceedings virtually allows the Court and an Appeal Board to hear any matter expeditiously, even if there are disruptive events, such as the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond national emergencies, where the circumstances of a particular case do not require the physical attendance of parties or their lawyers in the Court room, the presiding judge of the Court, or an Appeal Board, will assess the necessity and appropriateness of conducting the proceedings virtually on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether the convenience of virtual solemnisations could be extended to marriages where at least one party is overseas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While we recognise the convenience that this proposal may bring, we will need to study this carefully.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Under section 95(3) of AMLA, the Kadi must be satisfied that there is no lawful obstacle under Muslim law or AMLA to the intended marriage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, if the Kadi is unable to ascertain whether the party outside Singapore has legal capacity to contract the marriage, the conditions under this section will not be met.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similar to the requirements for the use of remote communication technology for the solemnisation of Muslim marriages under the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnisation and Registration of Marriages) Act 2020, currently, all parties to the intended marriage must be physically present in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This acts as a safeguard to ensure that all the conditions set out under Muslim law on the validity of the marriage and other legal requirements under section 95(3) of AMLA are fulfilled.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Digitalisation will not affect the fairness of the Court proceedings or the integrity of marriage solemnisations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is our resolve and assurance to Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC and ROMM will ensure that religious and customary practices are still fulfilled, and justice is served.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC and ROMM have adopted best practices and developed multiple safeguards to protect the propriety, solemnity, integrity and orderliness of digital proceedings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim expressed concern that the proposed amendments may change the manner of appeal hearings and the delivery of verdict by the Appeal Board which lawyers and parties have been accustomed to.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The concern is that allowing Court proceedings to proceed without oral hearings could affect the perception of justice being done, as parties could feel aggrieved as they are not able to witness in-person the "process" or how the Court arrives at an outcome.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The traditional mode of conducting proceedings synchronously by an oral hearing is still in place and will continue to be the default manner of proceedings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked what factors are considered when deciding that alternative modes of conducting proceedings are appropriate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This Bill will make available to SYC and Appeal Board the option of using electronic means of communication in place of physical attendance and the option to conduct proceedings in an asynchronous manner in place of an oral hearing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Asynchronous hearings, which are proceedings without an oral hearing, are typically allowed if the application is straightforward.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: An example would be where both parties consent to the application, or the application is made by one party but may be dealt with in the absence of the other party.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For such applications, an oral hearing is ordinarily not required because all relevant facts of the case have been submitted in affidavits, which is the primary mode of giving evidence to the Court.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Legal submissions will also unlikely be required for such cases.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Conducting the proceedings in an asynchronous manner would ordinarily not be appropriate where oral arguments are required from counsel or the litigants-in-person.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is typically the case for divorce hearings or trials, including an appeal hearing before the Appeal Board.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While an oral hearing is necessary in such cases, physical attendance of the counsel and the litigants-in-person may be dispensed with and the proceedings of the oral hearing may be conducted virtually where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin's query, the Court is not precluded from allowing the use of an alternative device in the midst of hearing should there be a technical difficulty as long as it is on an electronic communication platform approved by the Courts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about a situation where the Plaintiff has already given oral evidence but the Defendant fails or refuses to participate in further proceedings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For such cases, where oral evidence has been given, there are safeguards to protect the rights of both parties in the litigation process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Court will have to, first, assess whether the subsequent conduct of the hearing in an asynchronous manner will allow proceedings to be conducted fairly to both parties.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We agree with Ms Nadia Samdin that in setting up a dedicated venue to provide a centralised setting for online trials, we need to protect the vulnerable, such as those suffering domestic abuse cases, and ensure that they are able to make their cases fairly and free from intimidation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I want to reiterate that SYC will adopt alternative modes of conducting proceedings only where appropriate and facilitative.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since mid-2020, SYC has worked closely with members of the Bar on the implementation of electronic communication technology for Court proceedings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The common goal is to ensure that all SYC hearings that are conducted virtually are done in a just, secure and private manner, in accordance with the law and SYC's practice guidelines.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where there may be a serious risk of violence, separate courtrooms may be provided at SYC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is an additional measure on top of existing security protocols taken for all Court cases, such as Police presence at each Court hearing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The legal community welcomes this introduction of virtual proceedings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, Ms Shahirah Nassir, a lawyer at RW Law Practice, supports having proceedings held virtually.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While there were expected teething problems during the transitional period, such as video lag or audio quality issues, she felt that sessions were conducted on time and there were minimal technical issues faced.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More importantly, she found the platform to be a secure one that addresses security and privacy concerns in Court proceedings and the implementation of proceedings to be conducted remotely is in line with the numerous measures adopted by the Syariah Court to prioritise safety during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked how we will get the public on board on these changes, who may not find the changes intuitive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For its new digital system, SYC will establish a Helpdesk to provide users with technical support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC will also publish clear and complete user guidelines and videos on the SYC website.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The system is currently in the design stage and SYC will continue to work with partners and stakeholders to give litigants-in-person the necessary support and assistance they may need.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC and its bench of Judges will also continue to engage members of the Bar to help prepare all Court users for the upcoming changes in the second half of this year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This Bill also seeks to improve the legal processes relating to marriage and divorce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked who would be allowed access to the Register of Muslim Marriages and the Register of Revocation of Divorces.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is in line with who can access the Register of Marriages kept by ROM.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the Register of Muslim Divorces, the requesting party will be required to apply to SYC for a copy of an entry in the Register and must provide reasons to show sufficient interest in the matter.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is in line with the way similar information in the Family Justice Courts is protected.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The role of a hakam is described in section 50.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He is a person appointed by the Court to act for either the husband or the wife in divorce proceedings and will endeavour to effect a reconciliation and, if that is not possible, to facilitate an amicable resolution to the marital dispute.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, the amendment seeks to reduce acrimony and emotional hardship in such cases.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's query, in situations where one party creates an impasse by refusing to pay the hakam fees, the aggrieved party may seek redress from the Court at the hearing on ancillary matters to be reimbursed the payment that has been made on behalf of the defaulting party.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On a quite unrelated note, to Mr Faisal Manap's query on the non-payment of divorce fees, the Court has discretion to waive fees for reasons they deem acceptable, like the unaffordability of the party.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I fully agree with Mr Saktiandi Supaat that divorces are not to be taken lightly and the SYC strives to save marriages where it is possible to do so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There are various opportunities for a disaffected couple to work out their issues.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, parties are required to attend SYC's Marriage Counselling Programme, which was made mandatory at the last round of amendments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, after the divorce application has been filed in Court, parties attend a mediation session where they can still explore reconciliation options as well as areas of agreement for an amicable resolution to their marital dispute.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, parties may attend counselling or other family support activity or programme where they can receive support from professional counsellors and other social work professionals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to help couples work towards amicable resolutions where possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Next, let me address Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's query on what more is being done beyond these amendments for Muslim families going through divorce and non-Muslim families governed under the Women's Charter.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SYC works very closely with FJC and MSF to support Muslim families going through divorce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, SYC partners MSF to refer acrimonious cases to MSF's Divorce Support Specialist Agencies (DSSA) to help these families with Supervised Exchange and Visitations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF provides these referred Muslim families the same level of funding support given to non-Muslim families undergoing divorce under the auspices of the Women's Charter.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked who the "prescribed class of persons" may be under section 43A, where SYC may advise them, in addition to any of the parties or their children, to attend a family support programme or activity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We recognise that there may be other significant caregivers involved in a child's life, such as grandparents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The availability of family support programmes and activities is expanded to allow participation by such persons so that they may in turn help the child to better cope with his or her parents' divorce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin's query, the Programme for Children encompasses a range of possible support for children, including an assessment of the needs of the child and specific interventions, such as group programmes, counselling or psychological services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The assessment process will be used to make recommendations to parents on suitable interventions based on the needs of the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The overarching consideration is to work in the best interest of the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF and MCCY will continue to work closely with the relevant professionals to ensure that these evidence-based intervention programmes will benefit any child who needs help to cope with his or her parents' divorce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ultimately, parents are responsible for their child's well-being.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If they do not comply with the Court's advice, the Court will have the discretion to make any order it deems fit and, in relevant cases, may take the non-compliance of the parents into consideration in making custody, care and control and access orders, among other relevant factors, in determining the welfare of the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether the existing section 32(7) can meet our intent to allow Mufti to testify where a case is made on false doctrine.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sections 32(7) and 139(2) are significantly different in their scope and effect under the AMLA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think this was also referred to by Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is also not restricted to a request from a Court, as it can be made by any person.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the other hand, section 139(2) of AMLA relates specifically to evidence required for an offence of false doctrine and currently invokes a presumption in favour of the evidence given by the President of MUIS.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, the two sections have their own specific purpose under AMLA and the powers of the Legal Committee are not affected by the operation of section 139(2).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also continue to engage the community and religious fraternity to ensure that AMLA remains relevant for Muslims in Singapore.
